name: Atrophic Papulosis

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic porcelain-white atrophic papules with erythematous rim
Skin biopsy showing wedge-shaped dermal necrosis with thrombotic occlusion of small and medium-sized vessels
Exclusion of other causes of vasculopathy and coagulopathy
Evidence of systemic involvement such as gastrointestinal or central nervous system infarcts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic skin lesions and confirmatory histopathology with exclusion of other vasculopathies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and histopathological; systemic involvement worsens prognosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Porcelain-white atrophic papules with erythematous telangiectatic rim
searchTerms: white shiny skin bumps with red edges
porcelain-like papules with visible blood vessels
pale atrophic spots surrounded by redness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Wedge-shaped dermal necrosis on skin biopsy
searchTerms: triangle-shaped dead skin tissue on biopsy
wedge-shaped skin cell death seen microscopically
localized skin necrosis in wedge form

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain due to gastrointestinal infarctions
searchTerms: belly pain from gut tissue death
abdominal cramps due to intestinal infarction
stomach pain caused by blood flow loss
weakness or numbness due to cerebral infarcts
brain damage symptoms from blocked vessels

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be elevated
Normal coagulation studies in most cases
imaging: CT or endoscopy revealing gastrointestinal ulcerations or infarcts
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; possible sporadic or familial cases
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating wedge-shaped dermal necrosis and vascular thrombosis

distinguishingFeatures: Livedoid vasculopathy presents with painful ulcers and atrophie blanche but lacks porcelain-white papules
Histopathology shows fibrin thrombi without wedge-shaped necrosis
SLE has multisystem involvement with positive autoantibodies
Skin lesions differ and histopathology shows immune complex deposition

redFlags: Acute abdominal pain indicating gastrointestinal perforation or infarction
Rapid progression of skin lesions with systemic symptoms
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
Molloy ES, et al. Degos disease: a review. Curr Rheumatol Rep. 2019;21(10):53.
